analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 12: EDV inline, SZG confirms, BHP changes, RIO progressing, AAL and GLEN thoughts. Iron Ore on my mind
key_insights: China speculative accounts have started selling gold after earlier buying gold and selling copper. The author attributes it mainly to lingering Chinese demand concerns, with US rate hikes a secondary driver. Onshore feedback is that there is no demand pickup until 2Q27, and absent a policy catalyst the winter looks weak.

Iron ore fell 2% overnight to $90.40, after the move began in the Asian night session. Traders are selling physical iron ore on worries about hot onshore steel production. The open question is 2027 steel demand, which has run -2-3% YTD.

Steel supply and demand datapoints: MT sees destocking ending in Q4, US producers hold utilization at 77%, China steel exports fell in October to the lowest since April, and China onshore steel output is being discussed as possibly down 60-80mt in 2027. This comes as Simandou ramps up.

For a contrary iron ore view the author points to VALE US: a strong BRL tailwind, a base metals business whose value can be backed out, and 340mt of high grade iron ore that has so far avoided the CMRG dispute affecting the industry.

BHP named Adrian Wood as new CFO. He is well regarded by the market and was involved in building BHP's capital allocation framework (balance sheet, sustaining capex, dividends). BHP has heavy spend ahead, including a Vicuna FID by year end. The author has taken the over on time and cost at Vicuna.
The author still sees value in producers and says AAL LN is the top ask from the majority of clients.

GLC AU traded +4% relative, which the author attributes partly to iron ore weakness. Australian feedback is that investors want to buy the dip in copper and are increasingly worried about global steel production. The author expects more interest in AAL LN and GLEN LN on this pullback but not a similar move in London.

AAL traded on the Botswana diamonds update. In the MMG nickel bid for Brazil assets, MMG said it will leave no stone unturned to complete the deal. The EU antitrust decision deadline is December 21, 2026.

RIO asset sales: AFR reports binding offers in the first week of December. RIO has guided to $5bn of headline sales by year end, with Borates possibly $1-2bn. The author sees three issues: timing, size (could be large), and what RIO does with the proceeds. The author thinks it needs either a buyback structure or shovel-ready copper projects (McEwen Copper in Argentina, Taca Taca). Vicuna is not an option for RIO.

EDV LN fell about 7% with gold overnight, which the author thinks is too much. Q3 production was 256k oz (consensus 251k) and AISC was $1,857/oz (consensus $2,119). FY guidance is reiterated, with production tightened to the lower end of the range because of the Mana outage. Assafou FID capex was revised to $1.2bn from $1.06bn. Hounde production missed but AISC beat at Hounde and Ity, and Q4 grade will increase.
The Mana access ramp issue is two weeks old. The author sees it as a 2027 issue, with 2026 guidance met even at zero Q4 Mana output as open pit accelerates.

SZG GY opened -3% in a risk-off tape. VOE ended -7% the previous day on EU backdrop struggles. SZG pre-released on 22/10 (positive profit warning). Net debt guidance is below E800m (consensus E1.2-1.3bn), and PBT guidance is reiterated at E400-475m (previously E325-425m). The company cited energy costs and weak demand and EU recovery. Its results include a E150m impairment (tubes) and a E120m provision (restructuring and trading), and its NDA GY stake continues to support it. Contacts are not incrementally bullish on 2027. SZG is not covered at GS.
GP Guenter Papenburg AG (about 25.1% holder) with TSR Recycling is exploring a voluntary public takeover bid aimed at a consortium holding of at least 45% plus one share in SZG.

US steel is described as tight: producers are hedging, floating-price deals with typical 5-10% discounts on about 20% volume tolerance have tightened, and Cal27 at $1,250/st looks to have plateaued after a $100/st rally in October. Europe is strong, with the Turkish outage (largest Turkish exporter to Europe at about 4mt) tightening the market and about $50/st of contango.

GIR estimates value leakage from the CMRG discount negotiations at about $1bn a year. The base case is that CMRG will restart negotiations once finished, and iron ore is seen as a test case for other commodities, possibly bulks, base metals and copper.

FMG is in a standoff with CMRG and guidance depends on it ending. There is discussion of CMRG extending an embargo on FMG products, with no SSF (about 80mt) currently moving. Fortescue Blend is 58% grade at about 75mt, against BHP JBF at 60.5%.

The author is short iron ore names versus base metals (and says this is talking their own book). The reasons are low China steel exports, hot steel concerns onshore, CTAs fading the move and Simandou. FMG is the most obvious short, and RIO has a relatively high bar into year end on the asset sale process.
